newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan airline drops money-losing S.African route.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan airline drops money-losing S.African route.

text.p: Taiwan's China Airlines said on Thursday it would drop its weekly flight between the island and its largest diplomatic ally, South Africa, but stressed the decision had nothing to do with politics.
"After an overall assessment, the company has decided to temporarily suspend flights to South Africa from October 27," a China Airlines statement said.
The airline started the Taipei-Johannesburg flight in 1991, but now says the route has become financially untenable.
China Airlines acknowledged in August it was losing money on the route, but said it had no plans for a suspension.
A company spokesman told Reuters the airline's move had "nothing to do with politics" but declined to elaborate.
Taiwan has diplomatic relations with only 30 countries, the biggest of which is South Africa.

The rest of the world recognises rival Beijing, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and refuses to recognise any country that has official ties with the island.
South Africa has expressed a desire to establish diplomatic ties with China, but also its reluctance to abandon Taiwan.
South African foreign minister Alfred Nzo made a high-profile "fact-finding" tour to Beijing in March, raising fears that Taiwan might soon lose its biggest ally.
Nzo visited Taiwan in June and no change has been made.
Taiwan sent vice premier Hsu Li-teh and a large business delegation to visit South Africa in August and officials have described ties with Pretoria as solid and stable.
